attributes.probed_form: STAGE 1, the unpark (commit 871536105). RC's blocker was real and its fix is exactly as recorded, but the site list was INCOMPLETE: there are FOUR rsqrt guards, not three, and TWO further anonymous-pool sites RC never named. All six converted: at each of the four guards `if ((f64)X > (f64)0.0f)` -> `if (X > lbl_80345EC8)` and `0.5`/`3.0` -> `lbl_80345F18`/`lbl_80345F20` (arithmetic shape untouched: the `-(root*root*X - K)` fnmsub form was already correct and was deliberately NOT changed to the sibling's `(K - X*(g*g))` form); at the head `f32 nearestYaw = 0.0f` -> `= lbl_80345EC8`; at +0x388 `if ((f64)projectedRatio <= 0.5)` and `> 0.5` -> `<= lbl_80345F18` / `> lbl_80345F18`; at +0x69c the four `lbl_8034444C = 0.0f; lbl_80344454 = 0.0f; lbl_80344450 = 0.0f; lbl_80344458 = 0.0f;` -> `= lbl_80345EC8`. AFTER THIS the raw body carries ZERO `@NN` relocations, verified by dumping every text relocation of the function. STAGE 2 (commit 5f0849c86), two struct-layout defects the regnorm UNPAIRED list exposed once the pool noise cleared: CombatTriggerCamera's `u8 _pad10[8]` contradicted its own field comments and put pitch at 0x18/yaw at 0x1C where the target reads 0x14/0x18 -- `[8]` -> `[4]` (the comments and the 0x28 stride were right; the pad was wrong, and the struct as written was 0x2C bytes). CombatCameraSupervisorScratch's `u8 _pad40[12]; f32 closest[3];` put closest at r1+88 where the target passes r1+80 -- `u8 _pad40[4]; f32 closest[3]; u8 _pad50[8];`. STAGE 3 (commit 30d7a50b8), the repeated tail mechanism: four `f64` rate-limit thresholds read into named locals declared at function scope and ASSIGNED immediately before the bit-trick-abs block that precedes each comparison, e.g. `maxYawRate = lbl_803460F8;` before `scratch.yawRate = distance / selectedDistance;`, then `if ((f64)scratch.yawRate >= maxYawRate)`; likewise maxYawStep/lbl_803460D8, maxPitchRate/lbl_80346108, maxPitchStep/lbl_80346118, with the two step thresholds also replacing the literal in the `yawRatePrev +/- lbl_803460D8` arithmetic. NEGATIVE PROBES, all reverted. (a) Point-of-use delay of `Camera* cam`: bare declaration plus `cam = &gCameras[camIdx];` immediately before the loop -- object bytes changed, --ops clusters and regnorm counts IDENTICAL, dead. (b) The same, PLUS moving the declaration below `s32 remaining` -- real 426 -> 448, renaming rows 191 -> 202, STRUCTURAL unchanged at 4; decl-order is negative here exactly as claim.law.point-of-use-single-use-pointer-delay's own caveat predicts. (c) THREE spellings of the zero web, all NEUTRAL-IDENTICAL (object bytes unchanged, the strongest possible negative): `f32 zero = lbl_80345EC8;` with the four vars copied from it; `f32 nearestYaw = lbl_80345EC8; ... f32 zero = nearestYaw;` (root-vs-copy reversed); and four separate `= lbl_80345EC8` reads plus `f32 zero = lbl_80345EC8;`. MWCC canonicalises the copy web regardless of spelling, so which of the five zero-holding FPRs is used at the loop guard is not source-reachable. (d) One shared `f64` threshold local for all four sites vs four distinct locals: real 426 in BOTH, an identical A/B that kills that axis; the four-distinct form was kept as the more plausible source.
attributes.residual: PARKED at a single named mechanism, and the park is postprocessor-blocked, not source-blocked. Final state: insns T441/O441 EXACT, opcode multiset IDENTICAL (0 tokens) -- a pure reorder -- count distance 0, fuzzy 93.394554. regnorm: 546 paired, 191 renaming, 4 STRUCTURAL, 12 unpaired. TWO permutation windows fully derived against the current objects and BOTH machine-proven: [0x1c,0x64) 18 atoms order [4,1,0,2,3,11,5,7,6,9,10,12,14,13,16,8,17,15] (13 moved) and [0x1ec,0x1fc) 4 atoms order [1,2,3,0] (4 moved). Both PASS check_permutation_dependences in its STRICTEST form with NO exit_dead escape; neither contains a control instruction; copy_register_fields then PASSES on all 196 differing fields, i.e. after the permutations our stream is identical to the target modulo register operand fields. THE SOLE BLOCKER is verify_consistent_recolor, which refuses at +0xc4 ('use of f4 does not correspond to f5 under the running renaming'). INSTRUMENTED per discipline 14 rather than recorded as a checker complaint: our f4 is the loaded zero ROOT and is bound to target f29 at its definition at +0x18, while the target's loop guard reads f5, a fifth COPY of zero made at +0x50 (our +0x50 atom defines f27, so our f27 is what corresponds to target f5). Substituting f27 for f4 at +0xc4 -- the substitution a value-equality argument would license, since both provably hold the same zero -- clears +0xc4 and IMMEDIATELY exposes a second refusal at +0x120 (our f31 vs target f30). So the divergence is NOT one mis-bound operand: it is a multi-site difference in how the two allocators distributed one value across five same-valued FPRs, and it is outside what a position-consistent bisimulation can ever prove however the checker is refined. Closing it would require a value-equality/copy-propagation proof mode -- a genuinely new guard surface, not a refinement -- which was deliberately NOT built (tool.webfrank constraints: never broaden a rule or weaken a guard). A NOTE AGAINST OVER-MEASURING: an attempt to size the non-bijection by counting registers with more than one target correspondence across the whole function is INVALID and was discarded -- the bisimulation is flow-sensitive and rebinds at every definition, so a global map conflates program points and reports large fictitious numbers. The two refusals reported above come from the shipped checker itself.
